sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
ITC Limited, a diversified conglomerate, has undergone a significant development with the demerger of its Hotels Business into ITC Hotels Limited (ITCHL) effective January 1, 2025. ITCHL, with a 39.88% shareholding by ITC Limited, operates a substantial hospitality chain comprising over 140 properties and 13,000 rooms across six distinctive brands. The company's financial reporting is guided by Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), ensuring transparency and consistency in its consolidated financial statements. Revenue recognition is based on the transaction price for goods and services, with specific considerations for taxes, returns, and variable considerations.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for ITC Limited is centered on its diversified business portfolio and strategic restructuring efforts, such as the demerger of its Hotels Business. With ITCHL positioned as one of the fastest-growing hospitality chains in the country, we anticipate potential upside from this segment. However, without specific financial metrics such as revenue from operations or net profit after tax (PAT) provided in the excerpts, we cannot derive detailed financial ratios or comparisons. As such, our thesis is based on the company's strategic positioning and adherence to accounting standards, which suggest a commitment to transparency and operational efficiency. Further analysis of the company's financial performance and industry dynamics would be necessary to fully articulate an investment strategy.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body: ITC Limited is a diversified conglomerate with operations in various segments. The company's financials for FY24 and FY25 exclude the performance of the Hotels business, which was transferred to ITCHL on a going concern basis pursuant to a Scheme of Demerger. The financials for FY21 and FY22 were impacted by unprecedented disruptions in certain operating segments due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's revenue from operations for FY25 is ₹113,960 crore, with an EBITDA of ₹17,163 crore. The company's net profit margin for FY25 is 26.7%, with a return on net worth of 29.2%. However, the segment-wise revenue breakdown is not explicitly stated in the provided excerpts, making it challenging to provide a detailed segment analysis.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
ITC's financial performance for FY25 reflects a revenue from operations of ₹74,236.07 crore, a 10.3% increase from ₹67,292.60 crore in FY24. The company's total income for FY25 stood at ₹77,690.38 crore, up from ₹70,822.36 crore in the previous year. Net profit for FY25 was ₹20,091.85 crore from continuing operations and ₹35,195.61 crore including discontinued operations, compared to ₹19,910.23 crore from continuing operations and ₹20,421.97 crore including discontinued operations in FY24.

The company's financials for FY24 and FY25 exclude the performance of the Hotels business, which was transferred to ITCHL on a going concern basis pursuant to a Scheme of Demerger. Earnings per share (EPS) for FY25 were ₹16.07 for continuing operations and ₹28.15 including discontinued operations, compared to ₹15.98 for continuing operations and ₹16.39 including discontinued operations in FY24.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of ITC has outlined a corporate strategy focused on creating multiple drivers of growth, anchored on its core competencies, with a focus on three primary business groups: FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging, and Agri Business. As per the latest available data, the company's capital expenditure stood at ₹1,842.28 billion in 2025, with depreciation and amortization amounting to ₹1,668.88 billion. The FMCG segment, which includes cigarettes, branded packaged foods, and personal care products, accounted for a significant portion of the company's capital expenditure, with ₹836.32 billion spent in 2025. The management has also reported the company's revenue from external customers, with ₹65,635.22 billion generated within India in 2025.

The company's organisational structure and governance processes are designed to support effective management of multiple businesses while retaining focus on each one of them. The operating segments have been reported in a manner consistent with the internal reporting provided to the Corporate Management Committee, which is the Chief Operating Decision Maker. The management has also disclosed that the company is not reliant on revenues from transactions with any single external customer, with no single customer accounting for 10% or more of its revenues. sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
The recent developments at ITC have been marked by significant strategic initiatives and financial performance. As per the latest available data, the company's capital expenditure stood at ₹18.42 billion in 2025, with depreciation and amortization amounting to ₹16.69 billion. The FMCG segment, which includes cigarettes and other branded packaged foods businesses, accounted for a significant portion of the company's capital expenditure, with ₹8.36 billion and ₹5.16 billion spent in 2025 and 2024, respectively. The company has also reported revenue from operations within India of ₹65,635.22 crore in 2025, indicating a growth of approximately 9% over the previous year.

In terms of segment performance, ITC Infotech India Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company, recorded revenue from operations of ₹3,204.32 crore and a net profit of ₹466.62 crore in the year under review. The company has also expanded its global presence through the setup of subsidiary companies in various countries, including Brazil, Mexico, France, Germany, Italy, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia. sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for ITC is supported by the company's diversified business portfolio, with a presence in FMCG, Paperboards, Paper and Packaging, and Agri Business. The company's focus on creating multiple drivers of growth anchored on its core competencies is expected to drive long-term growth. Additionally, the demerger of the Hotels Business is likely to unlock value for shareholders, as evident from the exceptional gain of ₹15,163.06 crore recorded in FY 2024-25. The company's strong revenue growth within India, with revenue from external customers increasing to ₹65,635.22 crore in 2025 from ₹60,333.03 crore in 2024, also supports the bull case.

On the other hand, the bear case for ITC is centered around the company's dependence on a few key segments, such as FMCG and Paperboards, Paper and Packaging, which accounted for a significant portion of the company's capital expenditure and depreciation in 2025. The company's non-cash expenditure, excluding depreciation, also increased to ₹248.79 crore in 2025 from ₹202.53 crore in 2024, which could be a concern. Furthermore, the company's discontinued operations, including the Hotels Business, reported a significant exceptional gain in FY 2024-25, which may not be sustainable in the long term. Our base case assumes that ITC will continue to grow its revenue and profitability, driven by its diversified business portfolio and focus on core competencies, but at a moderate pace, with revenue from operations growing in line with historical trends. However, due to the lack of specific financial data on net profit and net worth in the provided excerpts, we are unable to provide a more detailed analysis of the company's profitability and financial position.

Principles of Consolidation The Group’s interests in its subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) in accordance with the relevant Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) specified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013. Subsidiaries (Ind AS 110) Line by line consolidation of the Statement of Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet is done by aggregating like items of assets, liabilities, income and expenses. The excess / deficit of the cost to ITC Limited of its investments in its subsidiaries over its share of net worth (residual interest in the assets of the subsidiaries after deducting all its liabilities) of the subsidiaries at the date of investment in the subsidiaries are treated as goodwill / capital reserve in the CFS. The goodwill is disclosed as an asset and capital reserve as a reserve in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Profit or loss and each component of other comprehensive income are attributed to the Group as owners and to the non-controlling interest; likewise the non-controlling interests in the net assets of the consolidated subsidiaries is identified and presented separately within Equity in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Inter-Company transactions within the Group (both Balance Sheet and Profit or loss items) are eliminated for arriving at the Group CFS. CFS is prepared applying uniform accounting policies of ITC Limited to the Group companies. Associates and Joint Ventures (Ind AS 28) An investment in associate and joint venture is initially recognised at cost on the date of the investment, and is inclusive of any goodwill / capital reserve embedded in the cost. Only share of net profits / losses and other comprehensive income of associates / joint ventures is considered in Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss. The carrying amount of the investment in associates / joint ventures is adjusted by the share of net profits / losses and other comprehensive income in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. 224 REPORT AND ACCOUNTS 2025 ITC Limited

Financial liabilities are derecognised when the liability is extinguished, that is, when the contractual obligation is discharged, cancelled or on expiry. Offsetting Financial Instruments Financial assets and liabilities are offset and the net amount is included in the Balance Sheet where there is a legally enforceable right to offset the recognised amounts and there is an intention to settle on a net basis or realise the asset and settle the liability simultaneously. Equity Instruments Equity instruments are recognised at the value of the proceeds, net of direct costs of the capital issue. Revenue Revenue is measured at the transaction price that the Company receives or expects to receive as consideration for goods supplied and services rendered, net of returns and estimates of variable consideration such as discounts to customers. Revenue from the sale of goods includes Excise Duties and National Calamity Contingent Duty which are payable on manufacture of goods but excludes taxes such as VAT and Goods and Services Tax which are payable in respect of sale of goods and services. Revenue from the sale of goods and services is recognised when the Group performs its obligations to its customers and the amount of revenue can be measured reliably and recovery of the consideration is probable. The timing of such recognition in case of sale of goods is when the control over the same is transferred to the customer, which is mainly upon delivery and in case of services, in the period in which such services are rendered. Government grants are recognised when there is reasonable assurance that the grant will be received upon the Group entity complying with the conditions attached to the grant. The Company is currently focused on three business groups : FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging and Agri Business. The Company’s organisational structure and governance processes are designed to support effective management of multiple businesses while retaining focus on each one of them. The Operating Segments have been reported in a manner consistent with the internal reporting provided to the Corporate Management Committee, which is the Chief Operating Decision Maker.
